body:
That you get those "extra" vertices compared to outlines is normal. Actual meshes with faces use triangles so you cant have a corner vertex without those edges connecting that vertex.

The polygons got changed from displaying the fake editor only outlines to displaying the actual meshes. Outlines alone are no valid geometry that can be used neither by the rendering or the physics collision. Previously they got converted behind the scene which surprised users when it did not work or when they noticed way too late how inefficient and broken the resulting geometry actually was at runtime. Now it displays the actual result including all the real geometry.

That the debug rendering manages to crash the mesh surface count is because it was changed to mesh rendering in a suboptimal way. It adds a new mesh surface for every single tiny shape to its debug quadrant mesh instead of a single mesh surface for all the combined shapes. That should be fixed because else it is rather easy to crash into the 256 max surface limit. It is also very inefficient and slow to render with so many surfaces.
